newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Six policemen wounded in Tamil rebel attack on petroleum depot in eastern Batticaloa.
Government to issue special identity card for residents of Jaffna peninsula over 10 years of age.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga sets up co-ordinating committee for northeast province headed by Shipping and Rehabilitation Minister M.H.M. Ashraff.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga appoints co-ordinating committee to oversee government activities in north-east province and overcome day-to-day problems of administration.
Navy destroys six Tamil Tiger rebel boats in three separate clashes off northeastern coast. More than 20 rebels believed to have been killed in battle.
Police hunt for three Tamil millionaires suspected to be helping Tamil Tiger rebels to smuggle arms and explosives into the capital Colombo. Arms distributed by gang operating autorickshaws.

Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and Treasury ask government to remove subsidy and raise fuel prices to offset loss of 1.6 billion rupees in first half of 1996 at state petroleum firm. Government plans to raise fuel prices in October, officials say.

Police probe activities of gang which tries to pursuade soldiers coming home on leave from the north and east not to return to war zone. Police say gang aims to disrupt military operations against Tamil rebels.
